facts.text: A data format is the agreed layout of a file that allows software to read it; versioning gives every file, setting and program a unique identifier so results can be traced to exactly what produced them.
facts.quote: A data format is the agreed way a file is laid out so that software can read it, and versioning is the practice of giving every file, setting and program a unique identifier so that any result can be traced back to exactly what produced it.

facts.text: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation), YAML and XML (extensible markup language) suit structured settings, configuration files, scenario descriptions and small tables, but not gigabytes of sensor data.

facts.text: Everything that can change a test result should have an immutable identifier recorded with each run, including the software build, calibration set, model weights, simulator and sensor-model version, terrain assets, scenario file and random seed; content hashes are recommended for this purpose.
